learning_outcomes.text: The student/graduate identifies and explains the graphic elements that constitute the general representation standards in industrial technical drawing.
The student/graduate identifies and explains the elements that define graphic calculation in industrial technical drawing.
The student/graduate identifies and explains the elements that together form the dimensioning module in industrial technical drawing.
The student/graduate identifies and explains the arrangement of views in industrial technical drawing.
The student/graduate explains how to create a sketch in industrial technical drawing.
The student/graduate explains how to create views, sections, and partial views in industrial technical drawing.
The student/graduate identifies and explains the representation, notation, and dimensioning of threads.
The student/graduate explains how to create an assembly drawing.
The student/graduate identifies and explains how to inscribe tolerances and surface finish on technical drawings.
The student/graduate uses classic instruments for graphic representations.
The student/graduate correctly represents the sketch of a part.
The student/graduate correctly uses dimensioning rules in industrial technical drawing.
The student/graduate defines and correctly represents the necessary sections in a mechanical part.
The student/graduate correctly uses representation, dimensioning, and positioning rules in creating an assembly drawing.
The student/graduate correctly uses both the rules for inscribing tolerances on technical drawings and those related to inscribing surface finish.

The student/graduate respects ethical principles, norms, and values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in decision-making for solving assigned tasks.
The student/graduate integrates into the work group and applies effective relationship and teamwork techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels.
The student/graduate permanently informs and documents oneself in their own field of activity by adequately using efficient lifelong learning methods and techniques.
The student/graduate develops professional projects in the field of engineering.

syllabus_topics: General norms used in industrial technical drawing: Lines, formats, title block, lettering used in industrial technical drawing. Solving these by CAD systems. Projection systems.
Geometric drawing notions: Graphic calculation in representing fillets and chamfers. Graphic calculation in representing the oval. CAD facilities for creating fillets and chamfers.
Dimensioning technical drawings: Characteristic elements of dimensioning. Dimensioning rules. Automation of the dimensioning process in CAD systems.
Arrangement of projections: First angle projection method. Third angle projection method.

Representation of views, sections, and partial views: Classification and representation of views. Representation of a sectioning path. Classification and representation of sections. Representation of the break line. Classification and representation of partial views.
Threads: Representation of threads. Dimensioning of threads. Notation of threads.
Assembly drawing: Representation rules in assembly drawing. Positioning rules in assembly drawing. Dimensioning rules in assembly drawing.
Surface finish: Basic symbol. Derived symbols. Rules for inscribing surface finish on industrial technical drawings.

Tolerances and dimensional deviations: Symbols used for indicating tolerances for form, position, and orientation deviations of surfaces. Rules for inscribing tolerances for form, position, and orientation deviations of surfaces on drawings. Rules and methods for inscribing dimensional deviations on technical drawings.
Occupational safety instruction in the laboratory. Presentation of works. Introductory notions of technical drawing.
Applications in geometric drawing.
Work 1 - Geometric constructions.
Exercises on arranging projections.
Making the sketch.
Sketching exercises in the notebook from parts with different degrees of difficulty.
Work 2 - Scaled drawing from a physical part.
Assembly drawing - sketches of component parts of an assembly, assembly sketch.
Work 3 - Assembly drawing.
Work 4 - Sketch of a part with medium difficulty.
Reworking assignments.
teaching_methods: Explanatory participatory lectures based on Power Point presentations

assessment_methods.method: Formative evaluation test on Geometric constructions
Formative evaluation test on drawing a scaled drawing of a simple mechanical part
Formative evaluation test on creating an assembly drawing
Summative evaluation test on drawing a scaled drawing of a medium complexity mechanical part

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the acquisition of the minimum learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of corresponding study credits. Conditions for promotion include the ability to correctly draw the projections of a mechanical part, with one of the views in section. Knowledge of basic dimensioning rules in industrial technical drawing and rules for representation, positioning, and dimensioning for assembly drawings are also required.
